newsitem.title: UK: Dollar sets 11-week high vs yen, hampered vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar sets 11-week high vs yen, hampered vs mark.

text.p: The dollar set an 11-week high against the yen after Japanese industrial output and retail sales reports overnight bolstered expectations that Japan's interest rates will stay near record lows for the time being.
The U.S. currency made less headway against the mark amid speculation the Bundesbank could switch to using variable rate tenders to set the securities repurchase rate.

Such talk was kept alive by comments Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick made in an interview with Germany's Handelsblatt newspaper. He said the Bundesbank had to balance a weak economy against a weak mark, the newspaper reported.

Koebnick added that the German central bank had made provision for sending a rate signal before its summer break. It fixed the repo rate at 3.0 percent for two weeks rather than the usual four weeks before its summer recess.

"Dollar/yen is bid as there is very good fundamental support for the dollar but no economic evidence that things are picking up in Japan," said Juergen Lindemann, senior trader at IBJ. By contrast, "dollar/mark is holding steady as people are focusing on the scope for interest rate moves in Germany."
Dollar/yen hit 118.75, its strongest since May 14. It was at 118.67/72 at 0745 GMT from 117.84/89 late Tuesday in Europe.
The dollar was at 1.8368/78 marks from 1.8314/24 yesterday and at 1.1512/22 Swiss francs from 1.5134/44 late Tuesday.
Reports on Wednesday showed Japanese industrial production fell 3.1 percent in June and that retail sales declined 2.3 percent in the same month.

While Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry predicted output would rise in the third quarter and that sales would pick up in July, traders are not expecting Japan's official discount rate to rise from 0.5 percent anytime soon.
"The pick up is so slow that interest rates are not going to go up for a while," said Lindemann at IBJ.

Though traders are not expecting an imminent rise in U.S. rates, the five-percentage-point premium American short rates already offer over their Japanese counterparts and demand for U.S. stocks and bonds are expected to bolster the dollar against the yen.
Traders are also expecting the dollar to claw back ground it lost to the mark yesterday after its surge to a seven-and-a-half-year peak of 1.8490 on Monday triggered profit taking.
"We tend to go up by the stairs and down by the lift these days but there is good demand for dollars after yesterday's correction and we should grind higher," said a trader in London.
Wariness that the Bundesbank could move to using variable-rate repos will only temporarily impede these gains, according to traders.
"Until they actually do something, I can't see any real reason to sell dollars," the London-based currency trader said.
U.S. data this week should also buoy U.S. assets and the dollar if they confirm the economy is growing at a healthy pace without stoking inflation, traders said.
The June new home sales report is due at 1400 GMT on Wednesday, but the focus is on second-quarter gross domestic product data on Thursday and the July jobs report on Friday.
